text: // Direct stderr writes remain visible when libtest captures passing tests.
The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that exercises evidence
authoring against a real configured Bedrock model when AWS credentials can be
loaded. It MUST skip before reading configuration or resolving credentials when
the `CI` environment variable is present. Outside CI, it MUST skip with a visible
warning when no Bedrock authoring configuration exists or the AWS SDK cannot load
credentials. Skip warnings MUST be visible under ordinary `cargo test` output.
`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, when set, MUST select a named authoring configuration for
the test. Otherwise the test MUST use the project's or user's selected
configuration when it selects Bedrock, falling back to the first named Bedrock
configuration in name order. Malformed configuration and invalid explicit
selections MUST fail the test. The selected profile, region, model, and options
MUST come from that configuration; credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK.
Once credentials load, model-request and authoring failures MUST fail the test
rather than be treated as skips. The test MUST exercise an additional source read
and judgment submission using a temporary project and stdout evidence output,
without changing the checkout's evidence. It MUST retain ordinary usage history
and check the returned evidence and recorded usage. Deterministic tests MUST
verify the CI and missing-credential skip paths without calling a model.

functions.rationale: Reviewed every selection branch against integration.live_bedrock_test and authoring.configuration_precedence. It loads typed user configuration, honors an explicit test configuration, otherwise uses the current project/user selection when it is Bedrock, and falls back in name order to another Bedrock configuration. Invalid explicit selections and parse failures propagate; absent default prerequisites can return None. These citations jointly account for test selection and reuse of the configured backend values; both declarations are selected.

functions.rationale: Reviewed subprocess isolation against integration.live_bedrock_test. The helper invokes only the live test, removes inherited AWS credentials and credential-source environment settings, installs isolated configuration paths, disables instance metadata, and points any mistaken model request at a closed local endpoint. Its citation covers the deterministic no-inference skip tests it supports; the selected declaration states that obligation.

functions.rationale: Reviewed each subprocess fixture and assertion against integration.live_bedrock_test. The test uses malformed configuration to prove CI skips before parsing, then absent configuration and an empty isolated AWS profile to verify visible prerequisite skips without inference. Malformed and explicitly missing configurations fail, and synthetic resolved credentials paired with an unreachable local endpoint prove that post-preflight provider errors fail rather than skip. The single requirement covers this verification matrix and is selected as an input.
